questions.stem: Your organization uses Microsoft Purview Audit (Standard) with no custom retention. How long are audit records retained by default?
options: 90 days
1 year
180 days
10 years
questions.explain: Audit (Standard) retains audit records for 180 days. One year is the Audit (Premium) default for Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive and Entra ID records, 10 years requires the add-on license, and 90 days applied only to logs generated before October 2023.

questions.stem: A SOC analyst must be able to search the audit log in the Microsoft Purview portal but must not change any audit configuration. Which role should you assign, following least privilege?
options: Audit Logs
View-Only Audit Logs
eDiscovery Manager
Compliance Administrator
questions.explain: View-Only Audit Logs allows searching and viewing the audit log without configuration rights. Audit Logs also permits managing audit settings, eDiscovery Manager is for eDiscovery cases, and Compliance Administrator is far broader than needed.

questions.stem: You suspect a compromised account created a mailbox rule to forward mail. Complete the Exchange Online PowerShell command to find inbox rules created by megan@contoso.com in the last 14 days.
options: -RecordType
-FreeText
-ObjectIds
-Operations
questions.explain: -Operations filters by the operation name, such as New-InboxRule. -RecordType filters by workload record type (not an operation), -FreeText does a text match, and -ObjectIds filters by the target object such as a SharePoint URL.

questions.stem: For each statement about audit log search in the Microsoft Purview portal, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: A search job keeps running if you close the browser.
An activity performed five minutes ago is guaranteed to appear in search results.
With Audit (Standard), you can export up to 50,000 rows from a search.

questions.explain: Audit searches run as jobs that continue after you close the browser and are kept for 30 days. Records from core services typically take 60 to 90 minutes to become available. The export limit is 50,000 rows for Standard and 1,000,000 for Premium.

questions.case: A script runs Search-UnifiedAuditLog for a seven-day window to export all FileDownloaded events for an investigation. It always returns exactly 100 records, although you know there are about 30,000.
questions.stem: What should you change to retrieve all the records with this cmdlet?
options: Add -HighCompleteness and set -ResultSize 50000
Add -Formatted so that AuditData is expanded
Use the same -SessionId with -SessionCommand ReturnLargeSet and repeat the call until no results return
Switch to Security & Compliance PowerShell, which has no result limit
questions.explain: Without -SessionCommand the cmdlet returns up to 100 records. ReturnLargeSet with a reused SessionId pages through up to 50,000 results (each call up to -ResultSize 5000). -ResultSize cannot exceed 5,000, -Formatted only changes display, and the cmdlet runs in Exchange Online PowerShell.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Purview Audit (Premium) event records the search terms a user entered in Outlook?
options: MailItemsAccessed
Send
SearchQueryInitiatedExchange
SearchQueryInitiatedSharePoint
questions.explain: SearchQueryInitiatedExchange logs searches in Exchange Online mailboxes (for example in Outlook). SearchQueryInitiatedSharePoint covers SharePoint searches, Send covers sent, replied and forwarded mail, and MailItemsAccessed records reads of mail items.

questions.stem: Users have E5 licenses with Advanced Auditing enabled, but no SearchQueryInitiatedExchange events appear for user lee@contoso.com. Complete the command that enables them.
options: -AuditAdmin
-AuditOwner
-AuditDelegate
-AuditLogAgeLimit
questions.explain: SearchQueryInitiated is added to the mailbox owner audit actions with -AuditOwner. -AuditAdmin and -AuditDelegate set actions logged for admins and delegates, and -AuditLogAgeLimit sets how long mailbox audit entries are kept, not which actions are logged.

questions.case: An attacker signed in to a finance mailbox from 203.0.113.50. MailItemsAccessed records from that IP and session include several Bind entries in Inbox and one Sync entry for the folder Invoices.
questions.stem: How should you scope the data exposure?
options: Treat only the Bind messages as accessed; Sync records are background activity and can be ignored
Treat the Bind messages, identified by InternetMessageId, and every item in the Invoices folder as accessed
Treat the entire mailbox as accessed because any MailItemsAccessed record means full compromise
Treat nothing as accessed until a Send event confirms exfiltration
questions.explain: A Bind record identifies an individual message by InternetMessageId. A Sync record covers a whole folder, so all items in that synced folder are assumed accessed. One folder sync does not by itself prove the whole mailbox was read, and data exposure does not depend on a Send event.

questions.stem: Which capabilities require Microsoft Purview Audit (Premium) rather than Audit (Standard)? Select THREE.
options: Searching the audit log with Search-UnifiedAuditLog
Logging Send events for mail users send, reply to or forward
Exporting search results to a CSV file
Retaining Exchange audit records for one year by default
Retaining audit records for 10 years with the add-on license
questions.explain: Send and other intelligent insights, the one-year default retention for Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive and Entra ID records, and 10-year retention (with the add-on) are Premium features. Both tiers support Search-UnifiedAuditLog and exporting results to CSV.

questions.stem: In March you create a 10-year audit log retention policy for executives who already have the 10-Year Audit Log Retention add-on. Which records will the policy keep for 10 years?
options: Records generated after the policy was created
All records still in the audit log, including those from January
Only records from non-user entities such as service principals
Only records that match a sensitivity label
questions.explain: Audit retention policies are not retroactive: they apply only to records generated after the policy is created. Records from non-user entities are kept for a fixed one year and are not affected by custom policies, and policies are not scoped by sensitivity labels.

questions.stem: In the current Microsoft Purview portal, where do you run a Content search to find every copy of a phishing email across all mailboxes?
options: In Microsoft Purview Audit, as a new search job
In Data lifecycle management, under retention labels
In Communication Compliance, as a new policy
In Microsoft Purview eDiscovery, as a search within a case
questions.explain: Content search functionality now lives in the new eDiscovery experience: you create a search in a case, including the system-generated Content Search case. Audit searches activity records, not message content; retention labels and Communication Compliance policies are not ad hoc content searches.

questions.stem: You need a KeyQL query that returns email items whose subject contains the exact phrase "Payroll update" and that were not sent by hr@contoso.com. Complete the query.
questions.code: kind:email AND subject:"Payroll update" AND ____ from:hr@contoso.com
options: NOT
not
NEAR
OR
questions.explain: Boolean operators in KeyQL must be uppercase, so AND NOT excludes the sender. Lowercase not is treated as a keyword, NEAR finds terms close together, and OR would broaden the results instead of excluding hr@contoso.com.

questions.stem: You are using Microsoft Purview eDiscovery to locate a malicious attachment across Exchange mailboxes. Put the steps in order.
options: Open an eDiscovery case and select Create a search on the Searches tab
Add the Exchange mailboxes as data sources
Build the query with the condition builder or KeyQL
Run the query and review the statistics and sample
Export the results or a report
questions.explain: Searches are created inside a case, then you add data sources, define the query, run it and check statistics and samples to confirm scope, and finally export results or a report for further investigation.

questions.stem: An analyst is a member of the eDiscovery Manager subgroup. A colleague created an eDiscovery case and did not add the analyst. What can the analyst do with that case?
options: Nothing: eDiscovery Managers can access only cases they created or are members of
View and export all searches in the case
Add herself to the case as a member
Remove members from the case
questions.explain: Members of the eDiscovery Manager subgroup see only cases they created or were added to. eDiscovery Administrators can access all cases and add themselves as members, and only administrators can remove case members.

questions.case: Your E3 tenant does not have Defender for Office 365 Plan 2. A member of the eDiscovery Manager role group created a search that finds a phishing email in 600 mailboxes. When she runs New-ComplianceSearchAction -Purge, PowerShell reports that no parameter matches the name Purge.
questions.stem: What should you do so the purge can run?
options: Assign her the eDiscovery Administrator role
Assign her the Search And Purge role
Add her to the Organization Management role group in the Exchange admin center
Add her to the Reviewer role group
questions.explain: Purging requires the Search And Purge role (found in the Purview Organization Management role group). eDiscovery Administrator does not include it, Exchange Online Organization Management membership is not sufficient, and Reviewer only grants access to review sets.

questions.stem: You need to remove a phishing message from mailboxes using Security & Compliance PowerShell. Put the steps in order.
options: Connect with Connect-IPPSSession -EnableSearchOnlySession
Create the search with New-ComplianceSearch
Run the search with Start-ComplianceSearch
Confirm the item count with Get-ComplianceSearch
Purge with New-ComplianceSearchAction -Purge
questions.explain: You connect to a search-only session, create and start the search, confirm the item count before deleting anything, and only then run New-ComplianceSearchAction -Purge. Status is then checked with Get-ComplianceSearchAction on the <search name>_Purge object.

questions.stem: Which statements about purging email with New-ComplianceSearchAction in a tenant without premium eDiscovery features are true? Select THREE.
options: A maximum of 10 items per mailbox is removed in one purge action
-PurgeType SoftDelete moves items to the Recoverable Items (Deletions) folder
It can also delete matching files from SharePoint and OneDrive
Items on litigation hold are permanently deleted
Unindexed items are not deleted
questions.explain: Each non-premium purge removes up to 10 items per mailbox, SoftDelete sends items to Recoverable Items (Deletions), and unindexed items are skipped. The action supports only Exchange Online mailboxes and public folders, and items on hold are preserved rather than permanently deleted.

questions.stem: You want to hunt for malicious Microsoft Graph API calls made by apps in your tenant. Which license is required to collect Microsoft Graph activity logs?
options: Microsoft Purview Audit (Premium)
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2
Microsoft Sentinel commitment tier
questions.explain: Microsoft Graph activity logs require a Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 tenant license plus an Azure subscription for the destination. Audit (Premium) and Defender for Cloud Apps are not the prerequisite, and Sentinel pricing tiers relate to ingestion, not to enabling the logs.

questions.case: Your SOC uses Microsoft Sentinel. You must be able to run KQL queries against Microsoft Graph activity logs and build analytics rules on them.
questions.stem: How should you configure collection?
options: Turn on Audit (Premium) and search the Graph operations in the Purview audit log
Create a diagnostic setting that sends Microsoft Graph activity logs to the Sentinel Log Analytics workspace
Create a diagnostic setting that archives Microsoft Graph activity logs to an Azure Storage account
Enable the Microsoft Graph Security API connector for alerts
questions.explain: Graph activity logs are streamed through diagnostic settings; sending them to a Log Analytics workspace creates the MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs table for KQL and Sentinel rules. Storage accounts suit long-term archive, not KQL. Purview audit does not hold these logs, and the Graph Security API connector ingests alerts, not request logs.

questions.stem: You want the apps, service principals and users with the most failed (401 or 403) Graph requests to /users over three days. Complete the KQL query.
questions.code:
MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs
| where TimeGenerated >= ago(3d)
| where ResponseStatusCode in (401, 403)
| where RequestUri contains "/users"
| ____ FailedRequests = count() by AppId, ServicePrincipalId, UserId
| sort by FailedRequests desc
options: project
extend
summarize
distinct
questions.explain: summarize applies the count() aggregation grouped by AppId, ServicePrincipalId and UserId. project and extend do not accept 'by' grouping with aggregates, and distinct returns unique combinations without counts.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Graph activity logs, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Security Administrator is the least-privileged role that can configure the diagnostic setting for Microsoft Graph activity logs.
You can join Graph activity logs to sign-in logs by matching SignInActivityId to UniqueTokenIdentifier.
You can filter out unwanted Graph request types directly in the diagnostic setting to cut costs.

questions.explain: Security Administrator is the least-privileged supported role for setting this up. SignInActivityId joins to UniqueTokenIdentifier in the sign-in log tables. Diagnostic settings do not support filtering; to reduce cost, use a workspace transformation on the table.
